exposure: timing of SARS-CoV-2 infection (early vs. late gestation)
outcome: SARS-CoV-2 IgG, IgM, and IgA receptor binding domain of the spike protein antibody concentrations
cohort: Mothers with SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy and their infants (dyads) were enrolled between July 2020 and May 2021.
finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection in early versus late gestation leads to a persistent antibody response in maternal blood, infant blood, and breast milk over the first 6 weeks after delivery, with early gestation infections associated with higher breastmilk IgA to spike protein and late infections with higher infant IgG levels to spike protein at 6 weeks.
